sub_answers.text: Relay takeover rules require that a foot of the second, third or fourth swimmer must be contacting the platform while (and before) the incoming teammate is touching the wall [d182796s1p0]. Relay starts can be in-motion for the starting swimmer, which saves approximately 0.6–1.0 seconds compared to a regular start [d182796s1p0]. Relay team order strategies commonly place the fastest swimmer last (anchor) and arrange the other three in orders such as second-fastest, third-fastest, slowest, then fastest; variations like slowest second or ascending speed order are also used [d182796s1p0]. Most competitive freestyle relay swimmers use the front crawl stroke in their freestyle legs [d182796s1p0].
